findings.summary: Maintenance commit does not bind proposals to the current workspace/brain/page context.
findings.details: The proposal carries workspaceId, brainKey, and pageKey, but commitMaintenanceProposal only checks revision and generation fields before returning a revision effect based on the proposal. A mismatched proposal object can therefore pass the pure commit seam and produce an effect for the wrong page/tenant if surrounding persistence code fails to compensate.

findings.summary: Commit-time lifecycle revocation is not enforced before accepting or publishing proposals.
findings.details: Gather and request reject revoked lifecycle state, but commitMaintenanceProposal does not re-check requireActiveLifecycle. Because lifecycle can change after proposal creation, a revoked context with matching generation can still accept a no-op or publish an Autopilot revision, contrary to the task requirement that lifecycle revocation fence revision effects.

findings.summary: Stale model/prompt proposal races can publish under a newer approved Autopilot pair.
findings.details: The task requires changed model/prompt pairs to downgrade to Review-first, but commit freshness ignores proposal.modelPromptPair and Autopilot eligibility is checked only against the current context. A proposal generated under an old pair can be published when context.modelPromptPair is now an approved pair and the numeric generations have not changed.
